title: Anthropic CEO Amodei Refutes Pessimistic Criticism, Says AI Trust Crisis Stems from Unfulfilled Promises

content_html:
As public discussions around AI risks and regulation continue to intensify, Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei recently publicly refuted criticism that he was conveying an overly pessimistic picture. This response directly addressed comments made by investor Gavin Baker on the All-In podcast and social media platform X, who argued that Amodei's warnings about AI dangers have fueled public opposition to AI infrastructure such as data centers in the United States, and claimed that he has "lost" in the AI regulatory debate, suggesting that he should demonstrate a more positive stance as an industry leader.

Amodei denied that his messaging had a negative tone, emphasizing that his article "Machines with Love" aimed to "balance risks and benefits," and was intended to compensate for the industry's lack of depiction of the potential of technology to improve the world.

He acknowledged that the general public holds a negative view of AI and that this is a significant issue, but strongly denied that this sentiment primarily stems from his or other leaders' warnings about risks, instead attributing it to a "fundamental trust crisis" - long-standing public distrust of businesses and governments, with the AI backlash being the latest manifestation of this deeper contradiction.

In response to external criticism, Amodei admitted that the core issue that should be focused on is not the messaging but the fact that companies like Anthropic "have yet to fulfill their grand promises to benefit the world."

On regulatory positions, Amodei rejected Baker's binary choice of "widespread dissemination vs concentration of power," pointing out that regulation is often seen by outsiders as a tool to counter corporate power. He revealed that Anthropic's policy recommendations have consistently avoided clauses beneficial to leading large companies, instead supporting smaller competitors, because he firmly believes that AI tends to concentrate power structurally, and open-weight models cannot fully address this issue. He believes well-designed rules can simultaneously address AI's catastrophic risks, institutional constraints on leading companies' power, and leave room for open-weight models.

content_html_zh:
随着围绕人工智能风险和监管的公众讨论不断加剧，Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 最近公开驳斥了有关他传达了过于悲观景象的批评。 这一回应直接回应了投资者 Gavin Baker 在 All-In 播客和社交媒体平台 X 上发表的评论，后者认为 Amodei 对 AI 危险的警告激起了公众对美国数据中心等 AI 基础设施的反对，并声称自己在 AI 监管辩论中“输了”，建议他作为行业领导者应该表现出更积极的立场。

阿莫迪否认他的信息带有负面基调，强调他的文章《充满爱的机器》旨在“平衡风险和收益”，并旨在弥补该行业缺乏描述技术改善世界的潜力。

他承认公众对人工智能持负面看法，这是一个重大问题，但他强烈否认这种情绪主要源于他或其他领导人对风险的警告，而是将其归因于“根本性信任危机”——公众对企业和政府长期存在的不信任，而对人工智能的强烈反对正是这一更深层次矛盾的最新表现。

在回应外部批评时，阿莫迪承认，应该关注的核心问题不是信息传递，而是像 Anthropic 这样的公司“尚未履行造福世界的宏伟承诺”这一事实。

在监管立场上，阿莫迪拒绝了贝克“广泛传播与权力集中”的二元选择，指出监管常常被局外人视为对抗企业权力的工具。 他透露，Anthropic的政策建议一贯避免有利于领先大公司的条款，而是支持规模较小的竞争对手，因为他坚信人工智能倾向于结构性权力集中，开放权重模型无法完全解决这一问题。 他认为，精心设计的规则可以同时解决人工智能的灾难性风险、对领先公司权力的制度约束，并为开放权重模型留出空间。
